213: /// Resolve the effective provider, model, temperature and token cap for a feature.
214: /// Matches `resolveFeatureConfig` in `src/utils/ai-client.ts`.
215: pub fn resolve_feature_config(
216:     settings: &AiSettingsRecord,
217:     feature: &AiFeature,
218: ) -> Option<ResolvedFeatureConfig> {
219:     let eligible: Vec<&AiProviderConfig> = settings
220:         .providers
221:         .iter()
222:         .filter(|p| p.supports_feature(feature))
223:         .collect();
224: 
225:     if eligible.is_empty() {
226:         return None;
227:     }
228: 
229:     let override_cfg = settings.per_feature.get(feature);
230: 
231:     let overridden = override_cfg
232:         .and_then(|ov| ov.provider_id.as_deref())
233:         .and_then(|id| eligible.iter().find(|p| p.id == id).copied());
234: 
235:     let preferred = overridden
236:         .or_else(|| {
237:             settings
238:                 .default_provider_id
239:                 .as_deref()
240:                 .and_then(|id| eligible.iter().find(|p| p.id == id).copied())
241:         })
242:         .or_else(|| eligible.first().copied())?;
243: 
244:     let model = override_cfg
245:         .and_then(|ov| ov.model.clone())
246:         .unwrap_or_else(|| preferred.default_model.clone());
247: 
248:     let temperature = override_cfg
249:         .and_then(|ov| ov.temperature)
250:         .unwrap_or_else(|| feature.default_temperature());
251: 
252:     let max_tokens = override_cfg.and_then(|ov| ov.max_tokens);
253: 
254:     Some(ResolvedFeatureConfig {
255:         provider: preferred.clone(),
256:         model,
257:         temperature,
258:         max_tokens,
259:     })
260: }

268:     persona_model: Option<&str>,
269:     persona_temperature: Option<f64>,
270: ) -> Option<ResolvedFeatureConfig> {
271:     let base = resolve_feature_config(settings, feature)?;
272: 
273:     let persona_provider = persona_provider_id
274:         .and_then(|id| settings.providers.iter().find(|p| p.id == id && p.supports_feature(feature)));
275: 
276:     let provider = persona_provider.cloned().unwrap_or(base.provider);
277: 
278:     let model = persona_model
279:         .map(String::from)
280:         .unwrap_or_else(|| {
281:             if persona_provider.is_some() {
282:                 provider.default_model.clone()
283:             } else {
284:                 base.model
285:             }
286:         });
287: 
288:     let temperature = persona_temperature.unwrap_or(base.temperature);
289: 
290:     Some(ResolvedFeatureConfig {
291:         provider,
292:         model,
293:         temperature,
294:         max_tokens: base.max_tokens,
295:     })
296: }

1: //! Managed local LiteRT-LM server lifecycle and child-process state machine.
2: //!
3: //! Authoritative reference: `desktop/litert-server.ts` and `desktop/main.ts`.
4: //!
5: //! When enabled via `TWYNE_DESKTOP_LOCAL_AI=true`, this manages the bundled
6: //! OpenBMB MiniCPM5 LiteRT-LM binary, imports the model if not already registered,
7: //! and starts the OpenAI-compatible loopback server on a free loopback port.
8: //!
9: //! Features:
10: //! - Bounded child-process execution and readiness probing (TCP connection attempts).
11: //! - Clean termination (SIGTERM / kill) on shutdown or drop to prevent orphan background servers.
12: //! - Non-blocking status inspections and health checks.
13: //! - Testable overrides for paths, timeouts, and poll intervals without modifying system environment.

81: /// Lifecycle state machine for the local LiteRT-LM server.

190: /// Find a free TCP port on loopback.
191: pub fn allocate_free_port(host: &str) -> io::Result<u16> {
192:     let listener = TcpListener::bind(format!("{host}:0"))?;
193:     let port = listener.local_addr()?.port();
194:     drop(listener);
195:     Ok(port)
196: }

198: /// Test whether a loopback port is currently accepting TCP connections.
199: pub fn is_port_accepting_connections(host: &str, port: u16, timeout: Duration) -> bool {
200:     let addr = format!("{host}:{port}");
201:     TcpStream::connect_timeout(
202:         &addr.parse().unwrap_or_else(|_| "127.0.0.1:0".parse().unwrap()),
203:         timeout,
204:     )
205:     .is_ok()
206: }

208: /// Check whether the local model is already registered in LiteRT-LM registry.
209: /// Runs `litert-lm list` and checks output whitespace tokens.
210: pub fn model_is_registered(bin: &Path, model_id: &str) -> Result<bool, LiteRtError> {
211:     let mut child = Command::new(bin)
212:         .arg("list")
213:         .stdout(Stdio::piped())
214:         .stderr(Stdio::null())
215:         .spawn()
216:         .map_err(|e| LiteRtError::RegistryCheckFailed(format!("Failed to spawn {} list: {e}", bin.display())))?;
217: 
218:     let mut stdout = child
219:         .stdout
220:         .take()
221:         .ok_or_else(|| LiteRtError::RegistryCheckFailed("Failed to open child stdout pipe".into()))?;
222: 
223:     let mut buffer = Vec::new();
224:     let mut chunk = [0u8; 4096];
225:     while buffer.len() < MAX_REGISTRY_OUTPUT_BYTES {
226:         let n = stdout.read(&mut chunk)?;
227:         if n == 0 {
228:             break;
229:         }
230:         buffer.extend_from_slice(&chunk[..n]);
231:     }
232: 
233:     let status = child.wait()?;
234:     if !status.success() {
235:         return Ok(false);
236:     }
237: 
238:     let output_str = String::from_utf8_lossy(&buffer);
239:     let registered = output_str
240:         .split_whitespace()
241:         .any(|token| token == model_id);
242:     Ok(registered)
243: }

245: /// Import the bundled model into LiteRT-LM registry under `model_id`.
246: pub fn import_model(bin: &Path, model_path: &Path, model_id: &str) -> Result<(), LiteRtError> {
247:     if model_is_registered(bin, model_id)? {
248:         return Ok(());
249:     }
250: 
251:     let model_str = model_path
252:         .to_str()
253:         .ok_or_else(|| LiteRtError::ImportFailed("Invalid UTF-8 model path".into()))?;
254: 
255:     let status = Command::new(bin)
256:         .args(["import", model_str, model_id])
257:         .stdout(Stdio::inherit())
258:         .stderr(Stdio::inherit())
259:         .status()
260:         .map_err(|e| LiteRtError::ImportFailed(format!("Failed to execute {} import: {e}", bin.display())))?;
261: 
262:     if !status.success() {
263:         return Err(LiteRtError::ImportFailed(format!("LiteRT model import exited with status {status}")));
264:     }
265:     Ok(())
266: }

268: /// Handle to the live LiteRT child server process.
269: /// Guarantees process termination on Drop or explicit `stop()`.
270: pub struct LiteRtServerHandle {
271:     pub port: u16,
272:     pub pid: u32,
273:     pub base_url: String,
274:     child: Arc<Mutex<Option<Child>>>,
275:     stopped: Arc<AtomicBool>,
276: }
277: 
278: impl LiteRtServerHandle {
279:     pub fn new(port: u16, pid: u32, base_url: String, child: Child) -> Self {
280:         Self {
281:             port,
282:             pid,
283:             base_url,
284:             child: Arc::new(Mutex::new(Some(child))),
285:             stopped: Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false)),
286:         }
287:     }
288: 
289:     /// Check if the child process is still running.
290:     pub fn is_alive(&self) -> bool {
291:         if self.stopped.load(Ordering::SeqCst) {
292:             return false;
293:         }
294:         let mut guard = self.child.lock().unwrap();
295:         if let Some(ref mut child) = *guard {
296:             match child.try_wait() {
297:                 Ok(None) => true,
298:                 _ => false,
299:             }
300:         } else {
301:             false
302:         }
303:     }
304: 
305:     /// Stop the server process gracefully, falling back to kill if needed.
306:     pub fn stop(&self) {
307:         if self.stopped.swap(true, Ordering::SeqCst) {
308:             return;
309:         }
310:         let mut guard = self.child.lock().unwrap();
311:         if let Some(mut child) = guard.take() {
312:             let _ = child.kill();
313:             let _ = child.wait();
314:         }
315:     }
316: }
317: 
318: impl Drop for LiteRtServerHandle {
319:     fn drop(&mut self) {
320:         self.stop();
321:     }
322: }

324: /// Bounded startup readiness state machine.
325: pub fn wait_for_server_ready(
326:     child: &mut Child,
327:     host: &str,
328:     port: u16,
329:     timeout: Duration,
330:     poll_interval: Duration,
331: ) -> Result<(), String> {
332:     let deadline = Instant::now() + timeout;
333: 
334:     while Instant::now() < deadline {
335:         // 1. Check if port is open and accepting TCP connections
336:         if is_port_accepting_connections(host, port, Duration::from_millis(50)) {
337:             return Ok(());
338:         }
339: 
340:         // 2. Check if child process exited prematurely
341:         match child.try_wait() {
342:             Ok(Some(status)) => {
343:                 return Err(format!("Server process exited before ready with status: {status}"));
344:             }
345:             Ok(None) => {
346:                 // Still running, sleep for poll interval
347:                 thread::sleep(poll_interval);
348:             }
349:             Err(err) => {
350:                 return Err(format!("Error polling server process: {err}"));
351:             }
352:         }
353:     }
354: 
355:     Err(format!("Server timed out after {}ms waiting for loopback port {port}", timeout.as_millis()))
356: }

358: fn current_time_ms() -> u64 {
359:     SystemTime::now()
360:         .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)
361:         .unwrap_or_default()
362:         .as_millis() as u64
363: }

365: /// High-level manager coordinating configuration, startup checks, port allocation,
366: /// child lifecycle, and shutdown.
367: pub struct LiteRtProcessManager {
368:     config: LiteRtConfig,
369:     state: LiteRtState,
370:     handle: Option<Arc<LiteRtServerHandle>>,
371: }
372: 
373: impl LiteRtProcessManager {
374:     pub fn new(config: LiteRtConfig) -> Self {
375:         let state = if config.enabled {
376:             LiteRtState::Stopped
377:         } else {
378:             LiteRtState::Disabled
379:         };
380:         Self {
381:             config,
382:             state,
383:             handle: None,
384:         }
385:     }
386: 
387:     pub fn state(&self) -> &LiteRtState {
388:         &self.state
389:     }
390: 
391:     pub fn config(&self) -> &LiteRtConfig {
392:         &self.config
393:     }
394: 
395:     pub fn is_ready(&self) -> bool {
396:         self.state.is_ready() && self.handle.as_ref().map_or(false, |h| h.is_alive())
397:     }
398: 
399:     pub fn base_url(&self) -> Option<&str> {
400:         self.state.base_url()
401:     }
402: 
403:     pub fn port(&self) -> Option<u16> {
404:         self.state.port()
405:     }
406: 
407:     /// Check if the running server is still alive. If it exited unexpectedly,
408:     /// transition state to `Failed`.
409:     pub fn poll_health(&mut self) -> &LiteRtState {
410:         if let LiteRtState::Ready { port, pid, .. } = self.state {
411:             let alive = self.handle.as_ref().map_or(false, |h| h.is_alive());
412:             if !alive {
413:                 self.state = LiteRtState::Failed {
414:                     stage: "runtime".to_string(),
415:                     reason: format!("Server process (pid {pid}, port {port}) died unexpectedly"),
416:                     timestamp_ms: current_time_ms(),
417:                 };
418:                 self.handle = None;
419:             }
420:         }
421:         &self.state
422:     }
423: 
424:     /// Start the local AI server following the authoritative Source protocol:
425:     /// 1. Check if enabled.
426:     /// 2. Validate asset files exist on disk.
427:     /// 3. Allocate free loopback port.
428:     /// 4. Verify/import model into LiteRT registry.
429:     /// 5. Spawn `litert-lm serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port <port>`.
430:     /// 6. Bounded poll for connection readiness.
431:     pub fn start(&mut self) -> Result<Option<String>, LiteRtError> {
432:         if !self.config.enabled {
433:             self.state = LiteRtState::Disabled;
434:             return Ok(None);
435:         }
436: 
437:         let bin_exists = self.config.bin_path.exists();
438:         let model_exists = self.config.model_path.exists();
439: 
440:         if !bin_exists || !model_exists {
441:             let state = LiteRtState::MissingAssets {
442:                 bin_exists,
443:                 model_exists,
444:                 bin_path: self.config.bin_path.clone(),
445:                 model_path: self.config.model_path.clone(),
446:             };
447:             self.state = state;
448:             return Ok(None);
449:         }
450: 
451:         let port = allocate_free_port(&self.config.host)
452:             .map_err(LiteRtError::Io)?;
453: 
454:         self.state = LiteRtState::CheckingRegistry;
455:         if let Err(err) = import_model(&self.config.bin_path, &self.config.model_path, &self.config.model_id) {
456:             let msg = err.to_string();
457:             self.state = LiteRtState::Failed {
458:                 stage: "import".to_string(),
459:                 reason: msg,
460:                 timestamp_ms: current_time_ms(),
461:             };
462:             return Err(err);
463:         }
464: 
465:         let mut child = Command::new(&self.config.bin_path)
466:             .args(["serve", "--host", &self.config.host, "--port", &port.to_string()])
467:             .stdout(Stdio::inherit())
468:             .stderr(Stdio::inherit())
469:             .spawn()
470:             .map_err(|e| LiteRtError::StartupFailed(format!("Failed to spawn local server: {e}")))?;
471: 
472:         let pid = child.id();
473:         self.state = LiteRtState::Starting {
474:             port,
475:             pid,
476:             started_at_ms: current_time_ms(),
477:         };
478: 
479:         if let Err(reason) = wait_for_server_ready(
480:             &mut child,
481:             &self.config.host,
482:             port,
483:             self.config.startup_timeout,
484:             self.config.startup_poll_interval,
485:         ) {
486:             let _ = child.kill();
487:             let _ = child.wait();
488:             self.state = LiteRtState::Failed {
489:                 stage: "readiness".to_string(),
490:                 reason: reason.clone(),
491:                 timestamp_ms: current_time_ms(),
492:             };
493:             return Err(LiteRtError::StartupFailed(reason));
494:         }
495: 
496:         let base_url = format!("http://{}:{port}/v1", self.config.host);
497:         let handle = LiteRtServerHandle::new(port, pid, base_url.clone(), child);
498:         self.handle = Some(Arc::new(handle));
499:         self.state = LiteRtState::Ready {
500:             port,
501:             pid,
502:             base_url: base_url.clone(),
503:         };

505:         Ok(Some(base_url))
506:     }

511:             handle.stop();
512:         }

87: struct TagMatch {

89:     end: usize,
90:     is_closing: bool,

93: /// Find occurrences of `<think...>` or `</think...>` or `<thinking...>` tags.
94: fn find_reasoning_tags(text: &str) -> Vec<TagMatch> {
95:     let mut matches = Vec::new();
96:     let bytes = text.as_bytes();
97:     let mut i = 0;
98: 
99:     while i < bytes.len() {
100:         if bytes[i] == b'<' {
101:             let start = i;
102:             let mut j = i + 1;
103:             // optional /
104:             let mut is_closing = false;
105:             while j < bytes.len() && (bytes[j] == b' ' || bytes[j] == b'\t' || bytes[j] == b'\n' || bytes[j] == b'\r') {
106:                 j += 1;
107:             }
108:             if j < bytes.len() && bytes[j] == b'/' {
109:                 is_closing = true;
110:                 j += 1;
111:             }
112:             while j < bytes.len() && (bytes[j] == b' ' || bytes[j] == b'\t' || bytes[j] == b'\n' || bytes[j] == b'\r') {
113:                 j += 1;
114:             }
115:             // check think or thinking
116:             let tag_name_start = j;
117:             while j < bytes.len() && (bytes[j].is_ascii_alphabetic() || bytes[j] == b'_' || bytes[j] == b'-') {
118:                 j += 1;
119:             }
120:             let name = &text[tag_name_start..j].to_ascii_lowercase();
121:             if name == "think" || name == "thinking" {
122:                 // find closing >
123:                 let mut end_found = false;
124:                 while j < bytes.len() {
125:                     if bytes[j] == b'>' {
126:                         let end = j + 1;
127:                         let tag_str = &text[start..end];
128:                         let norm = tag_str.replace(|c: char| c.is_whitespace(), "").to_ascii_lowercase();
129:                         let self_closing = norm.ends_with("/>") || norm.starts_with("</");
130:                         matches.push(TagMatch {
131:                             start,
132:                             end,
133:                             is_closing: is_closing || self_closing,
134:                         });
135:                         i = end;
136:                         end_found = true;
137:                         break;
138:                     }
139:                     j += 1;
140:                 }
141:                 if end_found {
142:                     continue;
143:                 }
144:             }
145:         }
146:         i += 1;
147:     }
148: 
149:     matches
150: }

159:     let matches = find_reasoning_tags(text);

164:     let mut visible = String::new();

168:     for m in matches {

171:         }
172:         if m.is_closing {
173:             depth = depth.saturating_sub(1);
174:         } else {
175:             depth += 1;
176:         }
177:         cursor = m.end;
178:     }

201:         }
202:         if m.is_closing {

204:         } else {
205:             depth += 1;
206:         }
207:         cursor = m.end;
208:     }

210:     if depth > 0 && cursor < text.len() {

217: fn clean_reasoning_whitespace(s: &str) -> String {
218:     let trimmed = s.trim();
219:     if trimmed.is_empty() {
220:         return String::new();
221:     }
222:     let lines: Vec<&str> = trimmed.lines().map(|l| l.trim_end()).collect();
223:     let mut result = String::new();
224:     let mut empty_count = 0;
225:     for line in lines {
226:         if line.is_empty() {
227:             empty_count += 1;
228:             if empty_count <= 2 {
229:                 result.push('\n');
230:             }
231:         } else {
232:             empty_count = 0;
233:             if !result.is_empty() && !result.ends_with('\n') {
234:                 result.push('\n');
235:             }
236:             result.push_str(line);
237:         }
238:     }
239:     result.trim().to_string()
240: }

274: /// Withhold any trailing fragment that could still become a reasoning tag.
275: /// Matches `trimPartialReasoningTag` in `reasoning-tags.ts`.
276: pub fn trim_partial_reasoning_tag(visible: &str) -> String {
277:     // Look for trailing `<` or `<t`, `<th`, `<thi`, `<thin`, `<think`, `<thinki`, etc.
278:     // or `</`, `</t`, `</th`, etc.
279:     if let Some(idx) = visible.rfind('<') {
280:         let suffix = &visible[idx..];
281:         let lower = suffix.to_ascii_lowercase();
282:         let is_prefix = matches!(
283:             lower.as_str(),
284:             "<" | "</"
285:                 | "<t"
286:                 | "</t"
287:                 | "<th"
288:                 | "</th"
289:                 | "<thi"
290:                 | "</thi"
291:                 | "<thin"
292:                 | "</thin"
293:                 | "<think"
294:                 | "</think"
295:                 | "<thinki"
296:                 | "</thinki"
297:                 | "<thinkin"
298:                 | "</thinkin"
299:                 | "<thinking"
300:                 | "</thinking"
301:         );
302:         if is_prefix {
303:             return visible[..idx].trim_end().to_string();
304:         }
305:     }
306:     visible.to_string()
307: }

311: const CONTRACT_TAGS: [&str; 3] = ["DOSSIER", "PROBE", "SYNTHESIZE"];
312: 
313: /// Withhold structured contract markers (DOSSIER/PROBE/SYNTHESIZE) and partial markers
314: /// from the chat stream.
315: pub fn filter_interview_stream_markers(raw_visible: &str) -> String {
316:     let lower = raw_visible.to_ascii_lowercase();
317: 
318:     // 1. Check full markers: e.g. "DOSSIER:", "\nDOSSIER:", etc.
319:     for tag in CONTRACT_TAGS {
320:         let marker = format!("{}:", tag.to_ascii_lowercase());
321:         if let Some(pos) = lower.find(&marker) {
322:             // Check if it's at start of string or preceded by newline / whitespace
323:             let valid_start = pos == 0 || raw_visible[..pos].ends_with('\n') || raw_visible[..pos].trim_end().is_empty();
324:             if valid_start {
325:                 return raw_visible[..pos].trim().to_string();
326:             }
327:         }
328:     }
329: 
330:     // 2. Check partial markers at the end of the string
331:     let trimmed_end = raw_visible.trim_end();
332:     if let Some(newline_pos) = trimmed_end.rfind('\n') {
333:         let last_line = trimmed_end[newline_pos + 1..].trim_start().to_ascii_uppercase();
334:         for tag in CONTRACT_TAGS {
335:             for len in 1..=tag.len() {
336:                 if last_line == tag[..len] {
337:                     return raw_visible[..newline_pos].trim().to_string();
338:                 }
339:             }
340:         }
341:     }
342: 
343:     raw_visible.trim().to_string()
344: }

383:     pub fn push(&mut self, input: GenerationStreamInput) -> GenerationStreamSnapshot {
384:         match input {
385:             GenerationStreamInput::TextDelta(delta) => {
386:                 self.raw_text.push_str(&delta);
387:                 self.text_started = true;
388:             }
389:             GenerationStreamInput::ReasoningStart => {

391:                 self.reasoning_ended = false;
392:             }
393:             GenerationStreamInput::ReasoningDelta(delta) => {

395:                 self.native_reasoning.push_str(&delta);
396:             }
397:             GenerationStreamInput::ReasoningEnd => {

399:             }
400:             GenerationStreamInput::Finish => {
401:                 self.reasoning_ended = true;
402:                 self.status = StreamRunStatus::Complete;
403:             }
404:             GenerationStreamInput::Error(_) => {
405:                 self.reasoning_ended = true;
406:                 self.status = StreamRunStatus::Error;

414:         let reasoning_parts = [
415:             self.native_reasoning.trim().to_string(),
416:             tagged_reasoning,

418:         let reasoning = reasoning_parts
419:             .iter()
420:             .filter(|s| !s.is_empty())
421:             .cloned()
422:             .collect::<Vec<String>>()
423:             .join("\n\n");

425:         let tagged_reasoning_running = has_open_reasoning_block(&self.raw_text);
426:         let reasoning_running = self.status == StreamRunStatus::Running
427:             && (tagged_reasoning_running
428:                 || (self.reasoning_started && !self.reasoning_ended && !self.text_started));
429: 
430:         let stripped = strip_reasoning_tags(&self.raw_text);
431:         let mut text = if self.status == StreamRunStatus::Running {
432:             trim_partial_reasoning_tag(&stripped)
433:         } else {
434:             stripped
435:         };
436: 
437:         if self.suppress_interview_markers {
438:             text = filter_interview_stream_markers(&text);
439:         }
440: 
441:         let active_part = if self.status != StreamRunStatus::Running {
442:             ActivePart::None
443:         } else if reasoning_running {
444:             ActivePart::Reasoning
445:         } else if self.text_started {
446:             ActivePart::Text
447:         } else {
448:             ActivePart::None
449:         };
450: 
451:         let text_status = if self.text_started && self.status == StreamRunStatus::Running {
452:             StreamPartStatus::Running
453:         } else if self.text_started {
454:             StreamPartStatus::Complete
455:         } else {
456:             StreamPartStatus::Pending
457:         };
458: 
459:         let reasoning_status = if reasoning_running {
460:             StreamPartStatus::Running
461:         } else if !reasoning.is_empty() {
462:             StreamPartStatus::Complete
463:         } else {
464:             StreamPartStatus::Pending
465:         };
466:

110:         let payload = Self::build_payload(req);

113:         let mut reader = BufReader::new(stream);
114:         let (status, headers) = parse_http_headers(&mut reader, req.timeout, &req.cancel_token)?;

116:         if status != 200 {

118:             return Err(AiError::HttpError {

124:         let body = read_all_body(&mut reader, &headers, req.timeout)?;

126:             .map_err(|e| AiError::MalformedResponse(format!("Invalid JSON: {e}")))?;

151:         &self,
152:         req: &CompletionRequest,
153:         mut on_snapshot: F,
154:     ) -> Result<CompletionResult, AiError>
155:     where
156:         F: FnMut(&GenerationStreamSnapshot) -> bool,
157:     {
158:         let mut stream_req = req.clone();
159:         stream_req.stream = true;
160:         let payload = Self::build_payload(&stream_req);
161: 
162:         let stream = self.connect_and_send("/v1/chat/completions", &payload, req.timeout, &req.cancel_token)?;
163:         let mut reader = BufReader::new(stream);
164:         let (status, _) = parse_http_headers(&mut reader, req.timeout, &req.cancel_token)?;
165: 
166:         if status != 200 {
167:             let mut line = String::new();
168:             let _ = reader.read_line(&mut line);
169:             return Err(AiError::HttpError {
170:                 status,
171:                 message: line.trim().to_string(),
172:             });
173:         }
174: 
175:         let mut accumulator = GenerationStreamAccumulator::new();
176:         let mut total_bytes = 0;
177:         let mut line_buf = String::new();
178:         let deadline = Instant::now() + req.timeout;
179: 
180:         while Instant::now() < deadline {
181:             if req.cancel_token.is_cancelled() {
182:                 return Err(AiError::Cancelled);
183:             }
184: 
185:             line_buf.clear();
186:             let n = reader
187:                 .read_line(&mut line_buf)
188:                 .map_err(|e| AiError::Timeout(format!("Stream read error: {e}")))?;
189: 
190:             if n > MAX_SSE_LINE_BYTES {
191:                 return Err(AiError::PayloadTooLarge(n));
192:             }
193: 
194:             if n == 0 {
195:                 // EOF reached
196:                 break;
197:             }
198: 
199:             total_bytes += n;
200:             if total_bytes > MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES {
201:                 return Err(AiError::PayloadTooLarge(total_bytes));
202:             }
203: 
204:             let trimmed = line_buf.trim();
205:             if trimmed.is_empty() || trimmed.starts_with(':') {
206:                 // Empty heartbeat line or comment
207:                 continue;
208:             }
209: 
210:             if let Some(data) = trimmed.strip_prefix("data:") {
211:                 let data_trimmed = data.trim();
212:                 if data_trimmed == "[DONE]" {
213:                     accumulator.push(GenerationStreamInput::Finish);
214:                     break;
215:                 }
216: 
217:                 if let Ok(chunk_val) = serde_json::from_str::<Value>(data_trimmed) {
218:                     if let Some(choice) = chunk_val["choices"].get(0) {
219:                         let delta = &choice["delta"];
220:                         if let Some(content) = delta["content"].as_str() {
221:                             accumulator.push(GenerationStreamInput::TextDelta(content.to_string()));
222:                         }
223:                         if let Some(reasoning) = delta["reasoning_content"].as_str() {
224:                             accumulator.push(GenerationStreamInput::ReasoningDelta(reasoning.to_string()));
225:                         }
226:                     }
227:                 }
228: 
229:                 let current_snap = accumulator.snapshot();
230:                 let should_continue = on_snapshot(&current_snap);
231:                 if !should_continue {
232:                     req.cancel_token.cancel();
233:                     return Err(AiError::Cancelled);
234:                 }
235:             }
236:         }
237: 
238:         if Instant::now() >= deadline {
239:             return Err(AiError::Timeout(format!("Stream timed out after {}ms", req.timeout.as_millis())));
240:         }
241: 
242:         let final_snapshot = accumulator.push(GenerationStreamInput::Finish);
243:         Ok(CompletionResult {
244:             text: final_snapshot.text.clone(),
245:             reasoning: final_snapshot.reasoning.clone(),
246:             snapshot: final_snapshot,
247:             raw_json: None,
248:         })
249:     }

251:     fn connect_and_send(
252:         &self,
253:         path: &str,
254:         payload: &str,
255:         timeout: Duration,
256:         cancel_token: &CancellationToken,
257:     ) -> Result<TcpStream, AiError> {
258:         if cancel_token.is_cancelled() {
259:             return Err(AiError::Cancelled);
260:         }
261: 
262:         let addr_str = format!("{}:{}", self.host, self.port);
263:         let addr = addr_str
264:             .parse()
265:             .map_err(|e| AiError::ConnectionRefused(format!("Invalid loopback address: {e}")))?;
266: 
267:         let mut stream = TcpStream::connect_timeout(&addr, timeout)
268:             .map_err(|e| AiError::ConnectionRefused(format!("Failed to connect to loopback {addr_str}: {e}")))?;
269: 
270:         stream
271:             .set_read_timeout(Some(timeout))
272:             .map_err(|e| AiError::ConnectionRefused(format!("Failed to set read timeout: {e}")))?;
273:         stream
274:             .set_write_timeout(Some(timeout))
275:             .map_err(|e| AiError::ConnectionRefused(format!("Failed to set write timeout: {e}")))?;
276: 
277:         let http_request = format!(
278:             "POST {path} HTTP/1.1\r\n\
279:              Host: {}:{}\r\n\
280:              Content-Type: application/json\r\n\
281:              Accept: text/event-stream, application/json\r\n\
282:              Content-Length: {}\r\n\
283:              Connection: close\r\n\
284:              \r\n\
285:              {}",
286:             self.host,
287:             self.port,
288:             payload.len(),
289:             payload
290:         );
291: 
292:         stream
293:             .write_all(http_request.as_bytes())
294:             .map_err(|e| AiError::Timeout(format!("Failed to write HTTP request: {e}")))?;
295: 
296:         Ok(stream)
297:     }
298: }

300: // ── HTTP Parsing Helpers ──
301: 
302: fn parse_http_headers(
303:     reader: &mut BufReader<TcpStream>,
304:     _timeout: Duration,
305:     cancel_token: &CancellationToken,
306: ) -> Result<(u16, Vec<(String, String)>), AiError> {
307:     let mut status_line = String::new();
308:     reader
309:         .read_line(&mut status_line)
310:         .map_err(|e| AiError::Timeout(format!("Failed to read HTTP status line: {e}")))?;
311: 
312:     if cancel_token.is_cancelled() {
313:         return Err(AiError::Cancelled);
314:     }
315: 
316:     let status_parts: Vec<&str> = status_line.split_whitespace().collect();
317:     if status_parts.len() < 2 {
318:         return Err(AiError::MalformedResponse(format!("Malformed status line: {status_line}")));
319:     }
320: 
321:     let status_code: u16 = status_parts[1]
322:         .parse()
323:         .map_err(|_| AiError::MalformedResponse(format!("Invalid status code: {}", status_parts[1])))?;
324: 
325:     let mut headers = Vec::new();
326:     let mut line = String::new();
327: 
328:     loop {
329:         line.clear();
330:         reader
331:             .read_line(&mut line)
332:             .map_err(|e| AiError::Timeout(format!("Failed reading headers: {e}")))?;
333: 
334:         let trimmed = line.trim();
335:         if trimmed.is_empty() {
336:             break;
337:         }
338: 
339:         if let Some((k, v)) = trimmed.split_once(':') {
340:             headers.push((k.trim().to_ascii_lowercase(), v.trim().to_string()));
341:         }
342:     }
343: 
344:     Ok((status_code, headers))
345: }

347: fn read_all_body(
348:     reader: &mut BufReader<TcpStream>,
349:     headers: &[(String, String)],
350:     _timeout: Duration,
351: ) -> Result<String, AiError> {
352:     let content_length = headers
353:         .iter()
354:         .find(|(k, _)| k == "content-length")
355:         .and_then(|(_, v)| v.parse::<usize>().ok());
356: 
357:     let mut body = String::new();
358:     if let Some(len) = content_length {
359:         if len > MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES {
360:             return Err(AiError::PayloadTooLarge(len));
361:         }
362:         let mut buf = vec![0u8; len];
363:         reader
364:             .read_exact(&mut buf)
365:             .map_err(|e| AiError::Timeout(format!("Failed to read {len} bytes: {e}")))?;
366:         body = String::from_utf8_lossy(&buf).to_string();
367:     } else {
368:         reader
369:             .read_to_string(&mut body)
370:             .map_err(|e| AiError::Timeout(format!("Failed reading body: {e}")))?;
371:     }
372: 
373:     Ok(body)
374: }

378: /// In-process mock loopback server for deterministically testing client behavior.
379: pub struct MockLoopbackServer {
380:     #[allow(dead_code)]
381:     listener: TcpListener,
382:     port: u16,
383:     shutdown: Arc<AtomicBool>,
384: }
385: 
386: #[derive(Clone, Debug)]
387: pub enum MockServerResponse {
388:     DirectJson(String),
389:     StreamSse(Vec<String>),
390:     ErrorStatus(u16, String),
391:     DelayedStream(Vec<String>, Duration),
392: }
393: 
394: impl MockLoopbackServer {
395:     pub fn spawn(response: MockServerResponse) -> io::Result<Self> {
396:         let listener = TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0")?;
397:         let port = listener.local_addr()?.port();
398:         let shutdown = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));
399:         let shutdown_clone = Arc::clone(&shutdown);
400: 
401:         let listener_clone = listener.try_clone()?;
402:         thread::spawn(move || {
403:             let _ = listener_clone.set_nonblocking(true);
404:             while !shutdown_clone.load(Ordering::SeqCst) {
405:                 match listener_clone.accept() {
406:                     Ok((mut stream, _)) => {
407:                         let _ = handle_mock_client(&mut stream, &response);
408:                     }
409:                     Err(ref e) if e.kind() == io::ErrorKind::WouldBlock => {
410:                         thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(10));
411:                     }
412:                     Err(_) => break,
413:                 }
414:             }
415:         });
416: 
417:         Ok(Self {
418:             listener,
419:             port,
420:             shutdown,
421:         })
422:     }
423: 
424:     pub fn port(&self) -> u16 {
425:         self.port
426:     }
427: 
428:     pub fn base_url(&self) -> String {
429:         format!("http://127.0.0.1:{}/v1", self.port)
430:     }
431: 
432:     pub fn stop(&self) {
433:         self.shutdown.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
434:     }
435: }
436: 
437: impl Drop for MockLoopbackServer {
438:     fn drop(&mut self) {
439:         self.stop();
440:     }
441: }

443: fn handle_mock_client(stream: &mut TcpStream, response: &MockServerResponse) -> io::Result<()> {
444:     let mut reader = BufReader::new(stream.try_clone()?);
445:     let mut line = String::new();
446: 
447:     // Read headers until empty line
448:     while reader.read_line(&mut line)? > 0 {
449:         if line.trim().is_empty() {
450:             break;
451:         }
452:         line.clear();
453:     }
454: 
455:     match response {
456:         MockServerResponse::DirectJson(json_str) => {
457:             let resp = format!(
458:                 "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\n\
459:                  Content-Type: application/json\r\n\
460:                  Content-Length: {}\r\n\
461:                  Connection: close\r\n\
462:                  \r\n\
463:                  {}",
464:                 json_str.len(),
465:                 json_str
466:             );
467:             stream.write_all(resp.as_bytes())?;
468:         }
469:         MockServerResponse::StreamSse(chunks) => {
470:             let headers = "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\n\
471:                            Content-Type: text/event-stream\r\n\
472:                            Connection: close\r\n\
473:                            \r\n";
474:             stream.write_all(headers.as_bytes())?;
475:             for chunk in chunks {
476:                 let sse_line = format!("data: {chunk}\r\n\r\n");
477:                 stream.write_all(sse_line.as_bytes())?;
478:                 stream.flush()?;
479:             }
480:             stream.write_all(b"data: [DONE]\r\n\r\n")?;
481:         }
482:         MockServerResponse::DelayedStream(chunks, delay) => {
483:             let headers = "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\n\
484:                            Content-Type: text/event-stream\r\n\
485:                            Connection: close\r\n\
486:                            \r\n";
487:             stream.write_all(headers.as_bytes())?;
488:             for chunk in chunks {
489:                 thread::sleep(*delay);
490:                 let sse_line = format!("data: {chunk}\r\n\r\n");
491:                 if stream.write_all(sse_line.as_bytes()).is_err() {
492:                     break;
493:                 }
494:                 let _ = stream.flush();
495:             }
496:             let _ = stream.write_all(b"data: [DONE]\r\n\r\n");
497:         }
498:         MockServerResponse::ErrorStatus(code, msg) => {

505:                  {}",

507:                 msg
508:             );
509:             stream.write_all(resp.as_bytes())?;

511:     }
512:

19: pub fn clamp_score(score: f64) -> u8 {

27: /// Strip Markdown code fences (` ```json ` or ` ``` `).
28: pub fn strip_json_fences(text: &str) -> String {
29:     let mut out = String::new();
30:     let mut in_fence = false;
31:     for line in text.lines() {
32:         let trimmed = line.trim();
33:         if trimmed.starts_with("```") {
34:             in_fence = !in_fence;
35:             continue;
36:         }
37:         out.push_str(line);
38:         out.push('\n');
39:     }
40:     out.trim().to_string()
41: }

43: /// Locate and extract the first balanced `{ ... }` JSON object.
44: pub fn extract_first_json_object(text: &str) -> Option<String> {
45:     let open = text.find('{')?;
46:     let mut depth = 0;
47:     let mut in_string = false;
48:     let mut escaped = false;
49: 
50:     for (i, ch) in text[open..].char_indices() {
51:         if escaped {
52:             escaped = false;
53:             continue;
54:         }
55:         if ch == '\\' && in_string {
56:             escaped = true;
57:             continue;
58:         }
59:         if ch == '"' {
60:             in_string = !in_string;
61:             continue;
62:         }
63:         if in_string {
64:             continue;
65:         }
66: 
67:         if ch == '{' {
68:             depth += 1;
69:         } else if ch == '}' {
70:             depth -= 1;
71:             if depth == 0 {
72:                 let end = open + i;
73:                 return Some(text[open..=end].to_string());
74:             }
75:         }
76:     }
77: 
78:     None
79: }

90: /// Extract tagged JSON block matching `tag: { ... }`.
91: pub fn extract_tagged_json(text: &str, tag: &str) -> Option<TaggedJsonSegment> {
92:     let lower_text = text.to_ascii_lowercase();
93:     let marker = format!("{}:", tag.to_ascii_lowercase());
94:     let marker_idx = lower_text.find(&marker)?;
95: 
96:     let search_start = marker_idx + marker.len();
97:     let open_rel = text[search_start..].find('{')?;
98:     let open = search_start + open_rel;
99: 
100:     let mut depth = 0;
101:     let mut in_string = false;
102:     let mut escaped = false;
103: 
104:     for (i, ch) in text[open..].char_indices() {
105:         if escaped {
106:             escaped = false;
107:             continue;
108:         }
109:         if ch == '\\' && in_string {
110:             escaped = true;
111:             continue;
112:         }
113:         if ch == '"' {
114:             in_string = !in_string;
115:             continue;
116:         }
117:         if in_string {
118:             continue;
119:         }
120: 
121:         if ch == '{' {
122:             depth += 1;
123:         } else if ch == '}' {
124:             depth -= 1;
125:             if depth == 0 {
126:                 let end = open + i + 1;
127:                 let json_slice = &text[open..end];
128:                 if let Ok(value) = serde_json::from_str::<Value>(json_slice) {
129:                     return Some(TaggedJsonSegment {
130:                         tag: tag.to_string(),
131:                         value,
132:                         start: marker_idx,
133:                         end,
134:                     });
135:                 }
136:             }
137:         }
138:     }
139: 
140:     None
141: }

143: /// Parse Rubric judge output, supporting both structured JSON and regex fallbacks.
144: /// Matches `parseJudgeOutput` in `src/utils/llm-parsing.ts`.
145: pub fn parse_judge_output(text: &str) -> Option<JudgeOutput> {
146:     let stripped = strip_json_fences(&strip_reasoning_tags(text));
147:     let candidate = extract_first_json_object(&stripped).unwrap_or_else(|| stripped.clone());

149:     if let Ok(val) = serde_json::from_str::<Value>(&candidate) {
150:         if let Some(obj) = val.as_object() {
151:             let score_val = obj.get("score").and_then(|v| v.as_f64());
152:             let rationale_val = obj.get("rationale").and_then(|v| v.as_str());

154:             if let (Some(s), Some(r)) = (score_val, rationale_val) {

165:         .lines()

167:             let lower = line.to_ascii_lowercase();
168:             if lower.contains("score") {
169:                 lower
170:                     .split(|c: char| !c.is_ascii_digit())
171:                     .find_map(|chunk| chunk.parse::<f64>().ok())
172:             } else {
173:                 None
174:             }
175:         });

177:     let rationale_opt = candidate
178:         .lines()
179:         .find_map(|line| {
180:             let trimmed = line.trim();
181:             if trimmed.to_ascii_lowercase().starts_with("\"rationale\"")
182:                 || trimmed.to_ascii_lowercase().starts_with("rationale:")
183:             {
184:                 Some(
185:                     trimmed
186:                         .trim_start_matches(|c: char| c != ':')
187:                         .trim_start_matches(':')
188:                         .trim()
189:                         .trim_matches('"')
190:                         .to_string(),
191:                 )
192:             } else {
193:                 None
194:             }
195:         });
196: 
197:     if let Some(s) = score_opt {
198:         return Some(JudgeOutput {
199:             score: clamp_score(s),
200:             rationale: rationale_opt.unwrap_or_else(|| {
201:                 "The draft does part of the work and leaves the rest to the writer.".to_string()

229: /// Parse array of ResearchTargets from model response text.

231: pub fn parse_research_targets(text: &str, max_targets: usize) -> Result<Vec<ResearchTarget>, String> {
232:     let stripped = strip_json_fences(&strip_reasoning_tags(text));

234:     // Try finding array `[ ... ]`
235:     let array_str = if let (Some(open), Some(close)) = (stripped.find('['), stripped.rfind(']')) {
236:         if open < close {
237:             &stripped[open..=close]
238:         } else {
239:             &stripped
240:         }
241:     } else {
242:         &stripped
243:     };
244: 
245:     let parsed: Value = serde_json::from_str(array_str)
246:         .map_err(|e| format!("Failed to parse JSON array of targets: {e}"))?;
247: 
248:     let items = parsed
249:         .as_array()
250:         .ok_or_else(|| "Parsed research targets root is not an array".to_string())?;
251: 
252:     let mut targets = Vec::new();
253:     for item in items.iter().take(max_targets) {
254:         let kind_str = item.get("kind").and_then(Value::as_str).unwrap_or("claim");
255:         let kind = match kind_str.to_ascii_lowercase().as_str() {
256:             "quote" => ResearchTargetKind::Quote,
257:             "work" => ResearchTargetKind::Work,
258:             "person" => ResearchTargetKind::Person,
259:             "statistic" => ResearchTargetKind::Statistic,
260:             "event" => ResearchTargetKind::Event,
261:             _ => ResearchTargetKind::Claim,
262:         };
263: 
264:         let anchor = item.get("anchor").and_then(Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default().trim();
265:         let query = item.get("query").and_then(Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default().trim();
266: 
267:         if !anchor.is_empty() && !query.is_empty() {
268:             targets.push(ResearchTarget {
269:                 kind,
270:                 anchor: anchor.to_string(),
271:                 query: query.to_string(),
272:             });
273:         }
274:     }

276:     Ok(targets)

188:     fn resolve_client(&self, provider_id: &str) -> Result<LoopbackClient, AiError> {

196:             })?;

198:         let base_url = provider.base_url.as_deref().unwrap_or_default();
199:         LoopbackClient::from_base_url(base_url).ok_or_else(|| {
200:             AiError::ConnectionRefused(format!("Invalid loopback base URL for provider '{provider_id}': {base_url}"))
201:         })
202:     }

204:     fn register_in_flight(&self, req: &CompletionRequest) {
205:         let mut guard = self.in_flight.lock().unwrap();
206:         guard.insert(
207:             req.request_id.clone(),
208:             InFlightEntry {

210:                 folio_id: req.revision.as_ref().map(|r| r.folio_id.clone()),
211:                 feature: req.feature.clone(),

213:             },
214:         );
215:     }

1: # Native AI Request/Runtime Adapter Foundation & Managed Local LiteRT Lifecycle
2: 
3: **Requirement Reference**: `desktop/gpui/PORT_PLAN.md` Requirement #24  
4: **Authoritative Source Implementations**:
5: - `desktop/litert-server.ts`
6: - `desktop/main.ts`
7: - `src/utils/ai-client.ts`
8: - `src/utils/desktop-bridge.ts`
9: - `src/utils/generation-stream.ts`
10: - `src/utils/reasoning-tags.ts`
11: - `src/utils/interview-stream.ts`
12: - `src/utils/llm-parsing.ts`
13: - `src/utils/research-targets.ts`
14: - `src/utils/background-research.ts`
15: - `src/utils/live-review.ts`
16: 
17: ---
18: 
19: ## 1. Managed Local LiteRT-LM Server Lifecycle
20: 
21: ### 1.1 Environment & Defaults Contract
22: The local model server is governed by the following environment variables:
23: | Environment Variable | Source Default | Description |
24: |---|---|---|
25: | `TWYNE_DESKTOP_LOCAL_AI` | unset (disabled) | `"true"` or `"1"` activates local LiteRT management. |
26: | `LITERT_LM_BIN` | `./bin/litert-lm` | Path to the LiteRT-LM CLI binary. |
27: | `LOCAL_MODEL_PATH` | `./models/MiniCPM5-2B_int4.litertlm` | Path to the bundled MiniCPM5 LiteRT weights. |
28: | `LOCAL_MODEL_ID` | `minicpm5-2b` | Stable model identifier registered in LiteRT. |
29: | `LOCAL_PROVIDER_ID` | `desktop-litert-local` | Stable provider identifier registered in settings. |
30: | `LITERT_LM_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_MS` | `20000` (20s) | Maximum deadline before readiness abort. |
31: | `STARTUP_POLL_MS` | `150` (150ms) | Loop interval checking TCP connectivity. |
32: 
33: ### 1.2 State Machine
34: The lifecycle follows a strictly bounded, non-blocking state machine:
35: ```mermaid
36: stateDiagram-v2
37:     [*] --> Disabled: TWYNE_DESKTOP_LOCAL_AI != true
38:     [*] --> CheckingAssets: TWYNE_DESKTOP_LOCAL_AI == true
39:     CheckingAssets --> MissingAssets: bin or model missing
40:     CheckingAssets --> CheckingRegistry: assets present
41:     CheckingRegistry --> ImportingModel: model not in registry
42:     CheckingRegistry --> Starting: model already in registry
43:     ImportingModel --> Starting: import exit status 0
44:     ImportingModel --> Failed: import exit status != 0
45:     Starting --> Ready: loopback port accepting TCP
46:     Starting --> Failed: child exit before ready / timeout
47:     Ready --> Failed: child exited unexpectedly
48:     Ready --> Stopped: explicit stop() or drop
49:     Starting --> Stopped: cancel or drop
50:     Stopped --> [*]
51: ```
52: 
53: ### 1.3 Child Process Invariants
54: - **Port Allocation**: Dynamically allocates a free TCP port by binding loopback `127.0.0.1:0`.
55: - **Registry Inspection**: Executes `litert-lm list` with a bounded stdout reader (capped at 256 KiB) to check for `minicpm5-2b`.
56: - **Graceful Termination**: The `LiteRtServerHandle` implements `Drop` to ensure any spawned child process is terminated on drop or exit. No orphan or zombie processes leak into the OS.
57: 
58: ---
59: 
60: ## 2. Native AI Request & Runtime Adapter
61: 
62: ### 2.1 Provider Configurations & Credentials Security
63: - **Server-Held Credentials**: API keys and authorization tokens are strictly encapsulated within the native runtime coordinator (`AiProviderConfig.api_key`).
64: - **No Token in UI**: Serialized records sent to UI or views omit API keys (`#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`), preventing credential exfiltration.
65: - **Provider Resolution**: Matches Source `resolveFeatureConfig` and `resolveFeatureConfigForPersona`:
66:   - Voice-only providers (`fishaudio`, `supertonic`) are constrained to voice features (`voice-narration`, `voice-transcription`).
67:   - Text and language features (`rubric-review`, `persona-analysis`, `research-extract`, etc.) route to language models.
68:   - Per-feature overrides in settings take precedence, falling back to global default provider.
69: 
70: ### 2.2 Keystroke & Manuscript Revision Isolation
71: - Whole-document AI jobs (such as Rubric reviews, synthesis, or background research) are tied to a `RevisionIdentity { folio_id, generation }`.
72: - When an AI response arrives, the coordinator validates if the manuscript generation has advanced during the request. Stale outputs are safely rejected rather than stomping live edits.
73: - Whole-document scans are kept away from per-keystroke typing paths.
74: 
75: ### 2.3 Streaming Accumulator & Reasoning Tags
76: - Implements `GenerationStreamAccumulator` matching `generation-stream.ts`.
77: - Text and reasoning channels have independent lifecycles (`active_part`: `Reasoning` | `Text` | `None`).
78: - Mid-stream reasoning tag withholding: trailing tag prefixes such as `<th`, `<think`, or `</thin` are held back via `trim_partial_reasoning_tag` to prevent visual flicker before the tag completes.
79: - Handles self-closing malformed closers (`<think/>`) and unclosed trailing blocks.
80: - Interview contract markers (`DOSSIER:`, `PROBE:`, `SYNTHESIZE:`) are withheld from visible chat bubbles.
81: 
82: ### 2.4 Loopback Transport (OpenAI-Compatible /v1)
83: - Zero external dependencies: communicates with `127.0.0.1:<port>/v1/chat/completions` using Rust's standard library `std::net::TcpStream`.
84: - Supports both non-streaming completions and streaming Server-Sent Events (`data: {...}`).
85: - Thread-safe `CancellationToken` enables immediate socket closure when the user switches folios or cancels an operation.
86: - Bounded line lengths (`MAX_SSE_LINE_BYTES = 64 KiB`) and bounded response bytes (`MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES = 8 MiB`).

1: /**
2:  * Desktop-only native LiteRT-LM server manager.
3:  *
4:  * When the desktop build is produced with local AI enabled
5:  * (`TWYNE_DESKTOP_LOCAL_AI=true`), this imports the bundled OpenBMB MiniCPM5
6:  * LiteRT-LM bundle into the local registry, then starts LiteRT-LM's
7:  * OpenAI-compatible server on loopback. The web app (loaded in the window)
8:  * discovers the endpoint via URL params and talks to it through the existing
9:  * `litert` provider — no model code ships in the browser bundle.
10:  *
11:  * Everything here is best-effort: if the flag is off or the binary/model are
12:  * not bundled, `startLocalAiServer()` returns null and the desktop runs as the
13:  * normal thin remote shell.
14:  */
15: import { spawn, type Subprocess } from "bun";
16: import { existsSync } from "node:fs";
17: import { createConnection, createServer } from "node:net";
18: import { resolve } from "node:path";
19: 
20: export interface LocalAiServer {
21:   port: number;
22:   stop: () => void;
23: }
24: 
25: const STARTUP_TIMEOUT_MS = Number.parseInt(
26:   process.env.LITERT_LM_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_MS ??
27:     process.env.LITERT_SERVER_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_MS ??
28:     "20000",
29:   10,
30: );
31: const STARTUP_POLL_MS = 150;
32: 
33: function enabled(): boolean {
34:   const v = process.env.TWYNE_DESKTOP_LOCAL_AI;
35:   return v === "true" || v === "1";
36: }
37: 
38: /** Resolve the bundled LiteRT-LM CLI path (overridable via env). */
39: function serverBinPath(): string {
40:   return resolve(process.env.LITERT_LM_BIN ?? "./bin/litert-lm");
41: }
42: 
43: const LOCAL_MODEL_ID = "minicpm5-2b";
44: 
45: /** Resolve the bundled MiniCPM5-2B LiteRT model path (overridable via env). */
46: function modelPath(): string {
47:   return resolve(
48:     process.env.LOCAL_MODEL_PATH ?? "./models/MiniCPM5-2B_int4.litertlm",
49:   );
50: }
51: 
52: /** Find a free TCP port on loopback. */
53: function freePort(): Promise<number> {
54:   return new Promise((res, rej) => {
55:     const srv = createServer();
56:     srv.once("error", rej);
57:     srv.listen(0, "127.0.0.1", () => {
58:       const addr = srv.address();
59:       const port = typeof addr === "object" && addr ? addr.port : 0;
60:       srv.close(() => res(port));
61:     });
62:   });
63: }
64: 
65: async function isPortAcceptingConnections(port: number): Promise<boolean> {
66:   return await new Promise((resolve) => {
67:     const socket = createConnection({ host: "127.0.0.1", port });
68:     let settled = false;
69: 
70:     const finish = (ready: boolean) => {
71:       if (settled) return;
72:       settled = true;
73:       socket.destroy();
74:       resolve(ready);
75:     };
76: 
77:     socket.once("connect", () => finish(true));
78:     socket.once("error", () => finish(false));
79:   });
80: }
81: 
82: async function waitForServerReady(
83:   proc: Subprocess,
84:   port: number,
85: ): Promise<"ready" | "exited" | "timeout"> {
86:   const deadline = Date.now() + STARTUP_TIMEOUT_MS;
87: 
88:   while (Date.now() < deadline) {
89:     if (await isPortAcceptingConnections(port)) {
90:       return "ready";
91:     }
92: 
93:     const exited = await Promise.race([
94:       proc.exited.then(
95:         () => true,
96:         () => true,
97:       ),
98:       Bun.sleep(STARTUP_POLL_MS).then(() => false),
99:     ]);
100:     if (exited) return "exited";
101:   }
102: 
103:   return "timeout";
104: }
105: 
106: /** Check whether LiteRT-LM already has the Twyne model in its registry. */
107: async function modelIsRegistered(bin: string): Promise<boolean> {
108:   let proc: Subprocess;
109:   try {
110:     proc = spawn({ cmd: [bin, "list"], stdout: "pipe", stderr: "ignore" });
111:   } catch {
112:     return false;
113:   }
114: 
115:   const output =
116:     proc.stdout && typeof proc.stdout !== "number"
117:       ? await new Response(proc.stdout).text()
118:       : "";
119:   const exitCode = await proc.exited;
120:   return (
121:     exitCode === 0 &&
122:     output.split(/\s+/).some((value) => value === LOCAL_MODEL_ID)
123:   );
124: }
125: 
126: /** Register the bundled model under the id sent by Twyne's OpenAI client. */
127: async function importModel(bin: string, model: string): Promise<boolean> {
128:   if (await modelIsRegistered(bin)) return true;
129: 
130:   let proc: Subprocess;
131:   try {
132:     proc = spawn({
133:       cmd: [bin, "import", model, LOCAL_MODEL_ID],
134:       stdout: "inherit",
135:       stderr: "inherit",
136:     });
137:   } catch (err) {
138:     console.error("[twyne:litert] failed to import local model:", err);
139:     return false;
140:   }
141: 
142:   const exitCode = await proc.exited;
143:   if (exitCode !== 0) {
144:     console.error(`[twyne:litert] model import exited with status ${exitCode}`);
145:     return false;
146:   }
147:   return true;
148: }
149: 
150: /**
151:  * Start the local model server. Returns the live endpoint info, or null when
152:  * local AI is disabled or its assets are missing.
153:  */
154: export async function startLocalAiServer(): Promise<LocalAiServer | null> {
155:   if (!enabled()) return null;
156: 
157:   const bin = serverBinPath();
158:   const model = modelPath();
159:   if (!existsSync(bin) || !existsSync(model)) {
160:     console.warn(
161:       `[twyne:litert] local AI enabled but assets missing — bin=${existsSync(bin)} model=${existsSync(model)}; running as thin shell.`,
162:     );
163:     return null;
164:   }
165: 
166:   const port = await freePort();
167:   if (!(await importModel(bin, model))) return null;
168: 
169:   let proc: Subprocess;
170:   try {
171:     // LiteRT-LM serves models from its registry. The import above binds the
172:     // bundled file to LOCAL_MODEL_ID; `serve` exposes the OpenAI-compatible
173:     // /v1 API that the web app already speaks.
174:     proc = spawn({
175:       cmd: [bin, "serve", "--host", "127.0.0.1", "--port", String(port)],
176:       stdout: "inherit",
177:       stderr: "inherit",
178:     });
179:   } catch (err) {
180:     console.error("[twyne:litert] failed to spawn local server:", err);
181:     return null;
182:   }
183: 
184:   const status = await waitForServerReady(proc, port);
185:   if (status !== "ready") {
186:     try {
187:       proc.kill();
188:     } catch {
189:       /* already gone */
190:     }
191:     console.error(
192:       `[twyne:litert] local model server ${status} before it was ready on 127.0.0.1:${port}`,
193:     );
194:     return null;
195:   }
196: 
197:   console.log(`[twyne:litert] local model server on 127.0.0.1:${port}`);
198:   return {
199:     port,
200:     stop: () => {
201:       try {
202:         proc.kill();
203:       } catch {
204:         /* already gone */
205:       }
206:     },
207:   };
208: }

2: /** Same shape, non-global: `.test` on a `/g` regex carries `lastIndex` state. */
3: const REASONING_TAG_PROBE = /<\/?\s*think(?:ing)?\b[^>]*\/?\s*>/i;
4: 
5: /**
6:  * Did the model reach for the reasoning channel at all?
7:  *
8:  * A predicate, not a policy. Reasoning is an expected mode — some models open
9:  * a `<think>` block on every turn by template — so nothing here should be read
10:  * as grounds for discarding a reply. Generation paths regenerate only when
11:  * {@link stripReasoningTags} leaves nothing visible.
12:  *
13:  * Kept for the places that genuinely need to know: the eval harness, which
14:  * counts how often a candidate model reasons and whether a tag ever leaks past
15:  * the stripper into text a reader would see.
16:  */
17: export function hasReasoningTags(text: string): boolean {
18:   return REASONING_TAG_PROBE.test(text);
19: }
20: 
21: /**
22:  * Drop a trailing fragment that could still become a reasoning tag.
23:  *
24:  * Tags arrive split across chunk boundaries, so a chunk ending in `<th` is
25:  * ambiguous: it becomes `<think>` or it becomes prose. Painting it and
26:  * retracting it a moment later flickers, so mid-stream we withhold it. Only
27:  * meaningful while text is still arriving — a finished string has no next
28:  * chunk, and whatever trails it is what the model meant.
29:  */

226: function normalizeKind(k: unknown): ResearchTargetKind {
227:   switch (k) {

240: function hashToken(s: string): string {
241:   let h = 0x811c9dc5;
242:   for (let i = 0; i < s.length; i++) {
243:     h ^= s.charCodeAt(i);
244:     h = Math.imul(h, 0x01000193);
245:   }
246:   return (h >>> 0).toString(36);
247: }

249: function collectList(value: unknown): Array<Record<string, unknown>> {
250:   if (Array.isArray(value)) {
251:     return value.filter(
252:       (v): v is Record<string, unknown> =>
253:         !!v && typeof v === "object" && !Array.isArray(v),
254:     );
255:   }
256:   if (value && typeof value === "object") {
257:     const rec = value as Record<string, unknown>;
258:     for (const key of ["targets", "items", "results"]) {
259:       if (Array.isArray(rec[key])) {
260:         return collectList(rec[key]);
261:       }
262:     }
263:   }
264:   return [];
265: }

267: /**
268:  * Parse an extraction reply into normalized {@link ResearchTarget}s.
269:  * Drops entries that could not possibly drive a search and removes
270:  * duplicate anchor/query pairs so the watcher never researches the same
271:  * passage twice in one pass.
272:  */
273: export function parseResearchTargets(text: string): ResearchTarget[] {
274:   const cleanTarget = (candidate: string): ResearchTarget[] => {
275:     let data: unknown;
276:     try {
277:       data = JSON.parse(candidate) as unknown;
278:     } catch {
279:       return [];
280:     }
281:     const list = collectList(data);
282:     const seenAnchors = new Set<string>();
283:     const seenQueries = new Set<string>();
284:     const targets: ResearchTarget[] = [];
285:     for (const rec of list) {
286:       const anchor = typeof rec.anchor === "string" ? rec.anchor.trim() : "";
287:       const rawQuery = typeof rec.query === "string" ? rec.query.trim() : "";
288:       const query =
289:         rawQuery.length >= 3 ? rawQuery.slice(0, 160) : anchor.slice(0, 80);
290:       if (anchor.length < 3 || query.length < 3) continue;
291:       const anchorKey = anchor.toLowerCase();
292:       const queryKey = query.toLowerCase();
293:       if (seenAnchors.has(anchorKey) || seenQueries.has(queryKey)) continue;
294:       seenAnchors.add(anchorKey);
295:       seenQueries.add(queryKey);
296:       const reason =
297:         typeof rec.reason === "string" && rec.reason.trim()
298:           ? rec.reason.trim().slice(0, 240)
299:           : "Needs a verifiable source";
300:       const importance =
301:         typeof rec.importance === "number"
302:           ? Math.max(1, Math.min(5, Math.round(rec.importance)))
303:           : 3;
304:       targets.push({
305:         id: `k-${targets.length}-${hashToken(anchorKey)}`,
306:         kind: normalizeKind(rec.kind),
307:         anchor: anchor.slice(0, MAX_ANCHOR_CHARS),
308:         reason,
309:         query,
310:         importance,
311:       });
312:     }
313:     targets.sort((a, b) => b.importance - a.importance);
314:     return targets;
315:   };
316: 
317:   const stripped = stripJsonFences(stripReasoningTags(text));
318:   const firstObject = extractFirstJsonObject(stripped);
319:   if (firstObject) {
320:     const fromObject = cleanTarget(firstObject);
321:     if (fromObject.length) return fromObject;
322:   }
323:   const firstArray = stripped.indexOf("[");
324:   if (firstArray >= 0) {
325:     const maybeArray = stripped.slice(firstArray);
326:     try {
327:       if (Array.isArray(JSON.parse(maybeArray))) {
328:         return cleanTarget(maybeArray);
329:       }
330:     } catch {
331:       /* fall through */
332:     }
333:   }
334:   return [];
335: }
336: 
337: /* ── Dedupe across passes ───────────────────────────────────────── */
338: 
339: /** Stable identity for a target, used to avoid re-researching. */
340: export function targetKey(t: Pick<ResearchTarget, "kind" | "anchor">): string {
341:   return `${t.kind}|${t.anchor.toLowerCase().replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim()}`;
342: }
343: 
344: /**
345:  * Pick the targets that will do the most new work: excludes anchors
346:  * already covered in the bibliography or just researched, then takes the
347:  * first `budget` (the model ordered by importance).
348:  */
349: export function selectFreshTargets(
350:   targets: ResearchTarget[],
351:   opts: {
352:     budget: number;
353:     coveredKeys?: ReadonlySet<string>;
354:     recentKeys?: ReadonlySet<string>;
355:   },
356: ): ResearchTarget[] {
357:   const fresh = targets.filter(
358:     (t) =>
359:       !opts.coveredKeys?.has(targetKey(t)) &&
360:       !opts.recentKeys?.has(targetKey(t)),
361:   );
362:   return fresh.slice(0, Math.max(0, opts.budget));
363: }
364: 
365: /* ── Result ranking ────────────────────────────────────────────── */
366: 
367: /**
368:  * Rank the provider's returned sources for a single target. Provider-agnostic
369:  * ordering that prefers a source with a real snippet and an author or p
370:  * publisher label; the provider's own ordering breaks ties. The caller still
371:  * applies URL dedupe and the per-pass save budget.
372:  */
373: export function rankSourcesForTarget<
374:   T extends {
375:     url: string;
376:     snippet?: string;
377:     title?: string;
378:     author?: string;
379:     publisher?: string;
380:   },
381: >(sources: T[]): T[] {
382:   const scored = sources
383:     .map((source, index) => ({
384:       source,
385:       score:
386:         (source.snippet && source.snippet.trim().length >= 40 ? 1 : 0) +
387:         (source.author ? 0.5 : 0) +
388:         (source.publisher ? 0.5 : 0) +
389:         (source.title ? 0.25 : 0) +
390:         Math.max(0, 1 - index * 0.2),
391:     }))
392:     .sort((a, b) => b.score - a.score);
393:   return scored.map((s) => s.source);
394: }

215:   return `${origin}/api/tinker`;
216: }

218: /** Speaks and listens, but has no language model behind it. */
219: export function isVoiceOnlyProvider(type: AiProviderConfig["type"]): boolean {
220:   return VOICE_ONLY_PROVIDER_TYPES.includes(type);
221: }
222: 
223: /** Features that want a voice, not a mind. */
224: const VOICE_FEATURES: ReadonlySet<AiFeature> = new Set<AiFeature>([
225:   "voice-narration",
226:   "voice-transcription",
227: ]);
228: 
229: /** Voice-only providers that can also transcribe (ASR), not just narrate. */
230: const VOICE_ASR_PROVIDERS: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set(["fishaudio"]);
231: 
232: /** Can this provider serve the requested speech feature? */
233: function supportsVoiceFeature(
234:   type: AiProviderConfig["type"],
235:   feature: "voice-narration" | "voice-transcription",
236:   provider?: AiProviderConfig,
237: ): boolean {
238:   if (feature === "voice-narration") {
239:     return (
240:       type === "openai" ||
241:       isOpenAiCompatibleProvider(type) ||
242:       isVoiceOnlyProvider(type)
243:     );
244:   }
245:   // Audio-capable language models can transcribe by reading the recording as
246:   // a file. Google and local/OpenAI-compatible multimodal models use that
247:   // path; Anthropic-compatible endpoints are intentionally excluded because
248:   // the Messages API does not define an audio content block. Voice-only
249:   // providers must implement ASR explicitly (fishaudio does; the browser's
250:   // Supertonic voice is synthesis-only).
251:   return (
252:     type === "openai" ||
253:     isOpenAiCompatibleProvider(type) ||
254:     (provider ? isTinkerProviderConfig(provider) : false) ||
255:     type === "google" ||
256:     type === "litert" ||
257:     (isVoiceOnlyProvider(type) && VOICE_ASR_PROVIDERS.has(type))
258:   );
259: }
260: 
261: /** Can a provider type serve this feature's modality? */
262: export function providerSupportsFeature(
263:   type: AiProviderConfig["type"],
264:   feature: AiFeature,
265:   provider?: AiProviderConfig,
266: ): boolean {
267:   return VOICE_FEATURES.has(feature)
268:     ? supportsVoiceFeature(
269:         type,
270:         feature as "voice-narration" | "voice-transcription",
271:         provider,
272:       )
273:     : !isVoiceOnlyProvider(type);
274: }

276: async function createModel(
277:   config: AiProviderConfig,
278:   modelOverride?: string,
279: ): Promise<LanguageModel | null> {
280:   try {
281:     const modelId =
282:       modelOverride || config.defaultModel || config.availableModels?.[0] || "";
283:     if (!modelId) return null;
284:     if (isTinkerProviderConfig(config)) {
285:       const { createOpenAI } = await import("@ai-sdk/openai");
286:       const tinker = createOpenAI({
287:         apiKey: config.apiKey,
288:         fetch: providerFetch,
289:         baseURL: tinkerRelayBaseUrl(),
290:       });
291:       return openAiLanguageModel(tinker, config, modelId);
292:     }
293:     switch (config.type) {
294:       case "openai": {
295:         const { createOpenAI } = await import("@ai-sdk/openai");
296:         const openai = createOpenAI({
297:           apiKey: config.apiKey,
298:           fetch: providerFetch,
299:         });
300:         return openAiLanguageModel(openai, config, modelId);
301:       }
302:       case "anthropic": {
303:         const { createAnthropic } = await import("@ai-sdk/anthropic");
304:         const anthropicProvider = createAnthropic({
305:           apiKey: config.apiKey,
306:           fetch: providerFetch,
307:         });
308:         return anthropicProvider.chat(modelId);
309:       }
310:       case "anthropic-compatible": {
311:         const { createAnthropic } = await import("@ai-sdk/anthropic");
312:         const anthropicProvider = createAnthropic({
313:           apiKey: config.apiKey,
314:           fetch: providerFetch,
315:           baseURL: config.baseUrl,
316:         });
317:         return anthropicProvider.chat(modelId);
318:       }
319:       case "google": {
320:         const { createGoogleGenerativeAI } = await import("@ai-sdk/google");
321:         const googleProvider = createGoogleGenerativeAI({
322:           apiKey: config.apiKey,
323:           fetch: providerFetch,
324:         });
325:         return googleProvider(modelId);
326:       }
327:       case "openai-compatible": {
328:         const { createOpenAI } = await import("@ai-sdk/openai");
329:         const openai = createOpenAI({
330:           apiKey: config.apiKey,
331:           fetch: providerFetch,
332:           baseURL: config.baseUrl,
333:         });
334:         return openAiLanguageModel(openai, config, modelId);
335:       }
336:       case "deepseek":
337:       case "openrouter":
338:       case "ollama":
339:       case "zai":
340:       case "minimax": {
341:         const { createOpenAI } = await import("@ai-sdk/openai");
342:         const openai = createOpenAI({
343:           apiKey: config.apiKey || "local",
344:           fetch: providerFetch,
345:           baseURL: config.baseUrl,
346:         });
347:         return openAiLanguageModel(openai, config, modelId);
348:       }
349:       case "fishaudio":
350:       case "supertonic":
351:         // Voice only — there is no language model to build. Callers fall back
352:         // to the server path, which is the correct behaviour.
353:         return null;
354:       case "litert": {
355:         // Desktop-only native model exposed as an OpenAI-compatible server on
356:         // loopback by the Electrobun shell. No real key; baseUrl is the local
357:         // endpoint discovered from the desktop bridge.
358:         const { createOpenAI } = await import("@ai-sdk/openai");
359:         const openai = createOpenAI({
360:           apiKey: config.apiKey || "local",
361:           fetch: providerFetch,
362:           baseURL: config.baseUrl,
363:         });
364:         return openAiLanguageModel(openai, config, modelId);
365:       }
366:       default:
367:         return null;
368:     }
369:   } catch (err) {
370:     reportApplicationDiagnostic("twyne:ai-client:create-model", err);
371:     return null;
372:   }
373: }

375: /* ── Feature routing ────────────────────────────────────────────── */
376: 
377: /**
378:  * Resolve the effective provider + model + params for a feature.
379:  * Falls back to the global default provider when a feature has no override.
380:  */
381: export function resolveFeatureConfig(
382:   settings: AiSettings,
383:   feature: AiFeature,
384: ): {
385:   provider: AiProviderConfig;
386:   model: string;
387:   temperature: number;
388:   /** Only set when the writer asked for a cap in Settings. */
389:   maxTokens?: number;
390: } | null {
391:   const normalized = normalizeAiSettings(settings);
392:   if (normalized.providers.length === 0) {
393:     return null;
394:   }
395: 
396:   // A voice-only provider can serve the voice features and nothing else; an
397:   // LLM provider that can't speak is no use for narration. Narrow the pool
398:   // before picking, so a writer with (say) Anthropic for the room and Fish
399:   // Audio for the voices gets the right one for each without configuring
400:   // per-feature overrides by hand.
401:   const eligible = normalized.providers.filter((p) =>
402:     providerSupportsFeature(p.type, feature, p),
403:   );
404:   if (eligible.length === 0) return null;
405: 
406:   const override: AiFeatureOverride | undefined =
407:     normalized.perFeature[feature];
408:   // An explicit per-feature override wins, but only if it names a provider
409:   // that can actually do the job.
410:   const overridden = override?.providerId
411:     ? eligible.find((p) => p.id === override.providerId)
412:     : undefined;
413:   const preferred =
414:     overridden ??
415:     eligible.find((p) => p.id === normalized.defaultProviderId) ??
416:     eligible[0];
417:   if (!preferred) return null;
418:   const provider = preferred;
419: 
420:   return {
421:     provider,
422:     model: override?.model ?? defaultModelForFeature(feature, provider),
423:     temperature: override?.temperature ?? defaultTemperature(feature),
424:     maxTokens: override?.maxTokens ?? defaultMaxTokens(),
425:   };
426: }
427: 
428: /**
429:  * Like {@link resolveFeatureConfig}, but lets a persona override the provider,
430:  * model, and temperature. This is what lets each editor run on its own model
431:  * so the voices differ at the generation level, not just in the prompt.
432:  * BYOK/client path only — the Convex hosted path uses one picked provider.
433:  */
434: export function resolveFeatureConfigForPersona(
435:   settings: AiSettings,
436:   feature: AiFeature,
437:   persona: { providerId?: string; model?: string; temperature?: number },
438: ): ReturnType<typeof resolveFeatureConfig> {
439:   const base = resolveFeatureConfig(settings, feature);
440:   if (!base) return null;
441: 
442:   const normalized = normalizeAiSettings(settings);
443:   const personaProvider = persona.providerId
444:     ? normalized.providers.find((p) => p.id === persona.providerId)
445:     : undefined;
446:   const provider = personaProvider ?? base.provider;
447: 
448:   return {
449:     provider,
450:     model:
451:       persona.model ?? (personaProvider ? provider.defaultModel : base.model),
452:     temperature: persona.temperature ?? base.temperature,
453:     maxTokens: base.maxTokens,
454:   };
455: }
456: 
457: /**
458:  * Is there a client-side provider that can do *language* work?
459:  *
460:  * Voice-only providers are excluded deliberately. Callers use this to decide
461:  * whether to take the BYOK path at all, and several of them treat a BYOK
462:  * attempt that yields nothing as a hard error rather than falling back to the
463:  * server — so counting a Fish Audio key here would break the Cast panel for
464:  * anyone who configured voice but not an LLM.
465:  */
466: export function hasConfiguredAiProvider(
467:   settings: Partial<AiSettings> | AiSettings | null | undefined,
468: ): boolean {
469:   if (!settings) return false;
470:   return normalizeAiSettings(settings).providers.some(
471:     (p) => !isVoiceOnlyProvider(p.type),
472:   );
473: }
474: 
475: /** Is there a client-side provider that can speak or listen? */
476: export function hasConfiguredVoiceProvider(
477:   settings: Partial<AiSettings> | AiSettings | null | undefined,
478: ): boolean {
479:   if (!settings) return false;
480:   return normalizeAiSettings(settings).providers.some(
481:     (p) =>
482:       supportsVoiceFeature(p.type, "voice-narration", p) ||
483:       supportsVoiceFeature(p.type, "voice-transcription", p),
484:   );
485: }
486: 
487: /**
488:  * Whether the selected model should receive the recording itself rather than
489:  * being sent to a dedicated `/audio/transcriptions` endpoint.
490:  *
491:  * models.dev metadata is authoritative when present. The name fallback keeps
492:  * manually entered models such as Inkling and Gemma useful until their
493:  * provider catalog has been loaded.
494:  */
495: export function modelAcceptsDirectAudio(
496:   provider: AiProviderConfig,
497:   model: string,
498: ): boolean {
499:   const modalities = provider.modelModalities?.[model];
500:   if (modalities) {
501:     return (
502:       modalities.input.includes("audio") && modalities.output.includes("text")
503:     );
504:   }
505:   if (provider.type === "google" || provider.type === "litert") return true;
506:   const id = model.toLowerCase();
507:   return /(?:inkling|gemma|gemini|audio|omni)/i.test(id);
508: }
509: 
510: function defaultModelForFeature(
511:   feature: AiFeature,
512:   provider: AiProviderConfig,
513: ): string {
514:   if (
515:     feature === "voice-transcription" &&
516:     modelAcceptsDirectAudio(provider, provider.defaultModel)
517:   ) {
518:     return provider.defaultModel;
519:   }
520:   if (
521:     feature === "voice-narration" &&
522:     (provider.type === "openai" || isOpenAiCompatibleProvider(provider.type))
523:   ) {
524:     return "gpt-4o-mini-tts";
525:   }
526:   if (
527:     feature === "voice-transcription" &&
528:     (provider.type === "openai" || isOpenAiCompatibleProvider(provider.type))
529:   ) {
530:     return "gpt-4o-mini-transcribe";
531:   }
532:   if (provider.type === "fishaudio") {
533:     // Fish's v1 TTS contract documents s2-pro and s1. Keep the default on a
534:     // documented model rather than the retired s2.1-pro-free id.
535:     return feature === "voice-transcription" ? "asr-1" : "s2-pro";
536:   }
537:   return provider.defaultModel;
538: }

540: function defaultTemperature(feature: AiFeature): number {
541:   switch (feature) {
542:     case "rubric-judge":
543:       return 0.2;
544:     case "rubric-review":
545:       return 0.3;
546:     case "persona-analysis":
547:       return 0.5;
548:     case "room-synthesis":
549:       return 0.4;
550:     case "voice-narration":
551:     case "voice-transcription":
552:       return 0.4;
553:     case "citation-format":
554:       return 0.1;
555:     case "source-summarize":
556:       return 0.3;
557:     case "source-detect-missing":
558:       return 0.2;
559:     case "research-web-search":
560:     case "research-extract":
561:       return 0.2;
562:     default:
563:       return 0.4;
564:   }
565: }
